# Fixture: static_same_name

Two `static` functions named `helper`, one in `left/util.c` and one in
`right/util.c` (B-09). The files share a base name on purpose: Clang's USR
for a function with internal linkage holds only the base name of its file,
so both would get `c:util.c@F@helper` (checked with
`c-index-test-20 -index-file`). FR-003 criterion 1 requires two functions.
`callback` is declared `static` once in `shared.h` and defined in both
files: two functions again, although Clang gives both `c:shared.h@F@callback`.
`twice` is defined in the header and reached from both translation units:
one function.

| Function | Declared | Defined (lines) | Linkage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `helper` | — | `left/util.c` 3–5 | internal |
| `helper` | `right/util.c` 3 | `right/util.c` 9–12 | internal |
| `left_value` | `shared.h` 4 | `left/util.c` 7–9 | external |
| `right_value` | `shared.h` 5 | `right/util.c` 5–7 | external |
| `library_only` | `shared.h` 6 | never (declaration only) | external |
| `callback` | `shared.h` 7 | `left/util.c` 11–13 | internal |
| `callback` | `shared.h` 7 | `right/util.c` 14–16 | internal |
| `twice` | — | `shared.h` 8 (`static inline`) | internal |

`right/util.c` declares `helper` before defining it, with the brace on its
own line. The compilation database is generated by the test, with
`-I<fixture root>`.
